summary: Advice requested: slice burst pools and implement graceful degradation for mixed realtime-chat + bulk-embed workload
description: Issue summary: Customer sees intermittent but persistent 429s for low-latency chat sessions while large background embedding imports run concurrently. They are on a dedicated pool and want recommended configuration to avoid disrupting interactive sessions and to support graceful degradation for bulk workers. Impact: user-facing chat latency spikes and aborted responses; bulk jobs repeatedly throttle and backfill slowly. Request: guidance on splitting burst pools, refill intervals, priority lanes, and a recommended graceful-degradation strategy (fallback routing, soft-rejects) to keep chat alive during large ingestion windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In prod-us-west, start a background embedding import (multipart) at 300 concurrent upload streams using open-embed-large model from SynapticMaps' ingesters.
2) Launch 50 parallel low-latency chat clients that maintain persistent SSE/websocket streams using gpt-4o-mini with prompt length ~120 tokens and average reply 40 tokens.
3) Observe 429 response spikes on chat sessions within 5-15 minutes after ingest starts; embedding uploads see repeated 429s and long backoff cycles.
4) Reproduce consistently by toggling the ingest concurrency between 100 and 400 and observing correlation with chat 429 rates.
logs: sample 429 response headers: x-rate-limit-policy: tenant-burst; x-refill-window-ms: 60000; x-tenant-remaining: 0; x-tenant-reason: burst-credit-exhausted
edge-proxy logs show: keepalive probe requests counted against tenant burst bucket from k8s healthchecks at ~1 req/s per node
ingest coordinator logs: multipart upload workers performing preflight checks counted as requests prior to upload chunking; spike correlates with refill window boundary.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Asha Patel (reporter): Customer reports chat sessions returning 429s (soft) while their nightly ingest runs. They are on a dedicated pool with reserved GPUs. They request guidance to avoid user-visible failures.

2026-03-10 10:04 - Support (Liam Chen): Acknowledged. Can you share sample request IDs and the ingest orchestration pattern? Also please confirm whether healthchecks/sidecars are enabled on same tenant network.

2026-03-10 11:30 - Customer (SynapticMaps, Ops): Provided traces and said they use an orchestrator that ramps workers quickly for hourly backfills. Healthchecks are enabled; sidecars perform preflight and telemetry pings.

2026-03-11 08:45 - SRE (Rina Morales): Initial hypothesis: burst-credit exhaustion due to un-isolated background workers + counted preflights and health probes. Suggest split burst pools and configure priority lanes for SSE chat to be isolated from bulk ingress. Will test staged config on their dedicated pool.

2026-03-12 14:22 - Support (Liam Chen): Implemented temporary mitigation: decreased ingest concurrency to 120 and enabled 'priority:interactive' header on chat clients. Customer reports fewer chat 429s; bulk jobs slower but proceed. Planning recommended permanent changes below.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis #1: Unsplit burst token pool — both chat and embed workers draw from same tenant burst bucket leading to exhaustion when ingest spikes.
Hypothesis #2: Preflight/healthcheck requests counted as full request units causing continuous drain across refill windows.
Observed: x-tenant-remaining often transitions to zero aligned with ingest worker ramp boundaries and refill window boundary (60s).
Temporary proof-of-concept: adding 'priority:interactive' header caused router to weight chat requests to priority lane which had separate small burst reserve; chat 429s decreased by ~80% during POC.
resolution: Workaround applied: reduced ingest concurrency and added priority header for interactive services. This is not a long-term fix for customer.
Recommended config changes for dedicated pool (actionable):
- Configure split burst pools: create two tenant burst lanes: 'interactive' (small high-frequency reserve) and 'bulk' (large but low-priority reserve).
- Set refill windows: interactive refill window = 250ms token smoothing for low-latency; bulk refill window = 60s for large imports.
- Exempt internal healthchecks/preflight pings from tenant accounting (or route through internal service account with separate quota).

- Enable soft-degradation policy on interactive route: when 'interactive' lane is near exhaustion, route to a lighter model (gpt-4o-mini -> gpt-4o-small) rather than immediate 429, and fall back to cached prefix responses for repeated prompts.
- Recommend 'priority' request header and server-side enforcement in their client stack; document client SDK snippet to add header for real-time requests.
- Rollout plan: stage changes in a canary dedicated pool, monitor x-tenant-remaining and 429 rate for 48h, then promote.
Follow-ups: Create a product docs task to surface these recommended configs in Console; suggested Confluence/KB page created for customer-specific runbook.
